done.why: I got to 185 of 350 and couldn't find anywhere left to go. The dam, Canyon View, the flooded passages, the river ledge and the hole under the altar were all closed off. The only treasure I hadn't fully cashed in was the egg, and I had neither the tools nor the expertise to open it. The thief, who might have opened it for me, was already dead.

about: It's a cut-down Great Underground Empire: the white house, the cellar, a troll, the maze, the Cyclops and the thief's hideaway, plus a temple you can only get out of by praying. You collect treasures and put them in the trophy case. The edges of the map are fenced off with polite, funny notes (a dam closed for inspection, scenery closed for repairs, black floodwater, a river with no boat), so it plays like one tight loop around the thief and the Cyclops.

moments.note: The trap door crashed shut and someone barred it. It had me worried for a moment, but it was open again later.
Two blows finished the troll: first knocked out, then killed. Quick and satisfying.
'Bar bar ...' The Loud Room echoed my words back, and typing 'echo' fixed it.
The dam is boarded up: 'CLOSED FOR INSPECTION. -- The Management.' This place is smaller than I expected.
My load was too heavy for the torch, 'the sword not least of it'. Juggling weight came up a lot.
The altar hole wouldn't let me down ('can wait a little longer'). I thought I was trapped in the temple.
Praying at the altar sent me out to the forest, which solved the trap.
The chimney fits 'you, your lamp and one thing more, and not an inch besides.' A clear, fair rule.
Saying 'Odysseus' sent the Cyclops running through the east wall.
I killed the thief with only the nasty knife. Tense, and the treasures reappeared.
The egg can't be opened ('neither the tools nor the expertise'). With the thief dead, it seems those points are gone.
The key couldn't reach the grating lock from above, so the grating was no use from the forest.
I lost track of where I was in the maze after typing directions in a burst.
The river ledge needs a boat, and there isn't one. That was the last dead end.

wished: I wished I could open the jewelled egg once the thief was gone, or that something had warned me that killing him would lock those points away.
I wished I could get past the closed dam, the flooded passages or the river, because they felt like the rest of the score.
I wished I could climb the dangling rope back up from the Torch Room.
I wished the maze gave me a way to mark rooms so I could map it properly.

lines.line: A board is nailed across it: "FLOOD CONTROL DAM #3. CLOSED FOR INSPECTION. -- The Management." You leave the dam to its inspection.
lines.why: It was a funny way to tell me where the map ends, and it changed how I chose my goals.

lines.line: Somebody has sorted the near end of the rubble into neat heaps by size, smallest nearest.
lines.why: It's an odd detail that hints someone lives down here.

lines.line: You decide that whatever is down there has waited this long and can wait a little longer.
lines.why: It told me the hole wasn't the way out, which sent me looking for another exit and led me to try praying.

lines.line: The chimney has room for you, your lamp and one thing more, and not an inch besides.
lines.why: It stated a constraint clearly enough that I could plan around it.

lines.line: The cyclops, hearing the name of his father's deadly nemesis, flees the room by knocking down the wall on the east of the room.
lines.why: This was the key moment. It opened the Treasure Room and a shortcut home.

lines.line: As the thief dies, the power of his magic decreases, and his treasures reappear
lines.why: I won the hardest fight, and it paid out the chalice.

fun.why: The puzzles came in a satisfying chain: the troll, the echo, praying out of the temple, Odysseus, then the thief fight. The weight limits and the dead ends near the end slowed things down.

engagement.why: The score kept going up, so I always had a goal. Once the egg was locked and every edge was closed, my drive ran out.

difficulty.why: Most obstacles had a fair solution. The temple felt like a trap until praying got me out. I never found how to open the egg.

interestingness.why: The closed-off edges are written with character, and some new rules stood out: the chimney limit, the altar hole refusing me, and the cave-in heaps.

prose.why: The new lines are vivid and dry, especially the dam board, the sighing hole and the cold river. The old room descriptions are solid too.
